transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

I guess… work, mostly. They kind of made it sound like I had to come. At the warehouse, by the forklift, I’ll just sort of stop sometimes, like with my arms up, and people get all loud about it. The forklifts have that beeping, you know, like when they back up, and it gets stuck in my head, so I’ll do it back, or I’ll copy the hand signals because they’re doing them wrong sometimes—or not wrong, just… sharp.

And the boxes, I move them into little patterns. It makes sense when I’m doing it, like rows or corners, but then everyone starts yelling that I’m messing up the pallets. That’s probably why I’m here.

Have you noticed this kind of behavior—freezing up, repeating sounds or gestures, arranging things in patterns—since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently, say in the last months or years?

Not really since I was a kid, I don’t think. It’s more… it’s been going downhill for maybe 11 months. Around when I moved into that shared apartment closer to work and school.

I mean, the apartment has these thin walls, and everybody has different shoes, like you can tell who’s walking by the sound, which is not really what you asked. But yeah—around then. Last months, almost a year.

When you freeze up or repeat those movements and sounds, do you feel like you're doing it on purpose to relieve some inner tension or urge, or does it feel like it just happens to you without you being able to control it?

I don’t know if “on purpose” is the right word. Like, at work, by the forklift, I’ll just be there with my arms up and then I notice people staring, and the beeping is happening and I’m sort of doing it back before I think about it.

Same with the hand signals—people wave them around all sharp, and I’ll copy them, and then it turns into a whole thing. Or the boxes, I start putting them in these little patterns, rows and corners, and everyone’s yelling to stop, but by then it already feels like I’m in the middle of doing it. It’s not like I’m trying to bother anybody.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or felt certain that something unusual or threatening was happening to you that others didn't believe was true?

I don’t… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. Like, sounds are everywhere, you know? In the apartment, the walls are thin, and pipes make noise, and shoes in the hallway sound different depending on who’s walking.

But voices that nobody else can hear… I don’t know. I haven’t really, like, checked with people every time. Sometimes people say I’m reacting to stuff too much, but they also don’t listen carefully. And threatening—um… I don’t know. Work feels threatening when everyone starts yelling, but that’s not unusual, that’s just people yelling.

When you arrange the boxes into those rows and corners, do you feel like there's a specific reason or meaning behind it—like it needs to be done to prevent something bad, or because it reveals some hidden order—or is it just something that happens without any particular belief attached to it?

I don’t think it’s like… to stop something bad, exactly. It’s more that I’m already doing it before I can explain it.

Like at the warehouse, I freeze up by the forklift with my arms up, or I start copying the beeping and the hand signals, and then the boxes end up in these little rows or corners. People are yelling for me to stop, but I’m still moving them around, like I can’t get back to the normal way fast enough.

I don’t know if there’s a meaning. It just kind of happens, and then everyone acts like I did it on purpose.

When you're frozen with your arms up like that, if a coworker tried to physically move your arms down or nudge you, would your body resist or stay stuck in that position, or would you be able to move normally if you wanted to?

I mean, I don’t really know what my body would do exactly. People mostly yell before they touch me. It’s like by the forklift I’m just there with my arms up, and the beeping is going, and then I’m copying it, or copying the hand signals, and then somehow I’m moving boxes into these weird little rows and corners.

If someone nudged me, maybe I’d move, maybe not—I’m not thinking normal right then. Everyone’s shouting to stop, and I’m still doing the thing, like I’m stuck in the middle of it.

Yeah, I guess that’s… that’s why they brought me in, mostly. At the warehouse I keep doing stuff that doesn’t make sense to them, like freezing there by the forklift with my arms up, and then the beeping starts getting in my head—not in my head, I mean it’s the forklift beeping—and I’ll copy it, or copy the hand signals.

And then the boxes, I’ll start moving them into these little rows or corners, like patterns, even when everyone’s yelling at me to stop. It’s not like I’m trying to mess things up. It just happens, and then people get mad, and the supervisor starts looking at me like I’m dangerous or something.
Do these freezing episodes, the copying of sounds and gestures, or the box-arranging happen anywhere outside of work—like at home or with roommates—or do they only occur on the job?

Mostly it’s at the warehouse, I guess. That’s where people notice it because, you know, there’s the forklift and the beeping and everybody doing those hand signals, and then I’m just… standing there with my arms up, or I start copying it.

At home there aren’t really boxes like that, not the same way. I mean, I’ll put things down and move stuff around, but the thing they brought me in for is work—the rows and corners with the boxes, and people yelling at me to stop like I’m doing it on purpose. It happens there.
Have you had any recent medical problems—like a head injury, seizures, infections, thyroid issues, or new medications or drug/alcohol use—around the time these episodes started?

I don’t… I don’t think there was some big thing like that. I mean, I didn’t get hit in the head that I remember. At work you bump into stuff all the time, pallets and corners and whatever, but that’s just the warehouse, you know?

I’m not really sure about thyroid stuff. I don’t even know what that would feel like. And medications—no, I don’t think there was some new thing right when it started. I don’t really keep track like that.

Alcohol or drugs, no, not like… I mean, people talk about that like it explains everything, but I’m just going to work and then the whole place is beeping and moving and everyone’s mad. I don’t know. I don’t have a good medical answer for it.

Outside of these episodes at work, have you noticed any changes in yourself lately—like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, wanting to be alone more, or having trouble keeping your thoughts organized when you talk to people?

Yeah… I mean, talking to people has gotten weird. Like when my supervisor asks which pallets are supposed to go on the truck, I know I’m supposed to just say, you know, “those ones” or whatever, from the load sheet.

But then I start explaining and it goes… sideways. I’ll be talking about the load sheet, and then I’m thinking about the house I used to live in, because the paper had a corner torn like the wallpaper there, and then I’m talking about fishing with my uncle, and then somehow church boxes, like the boxes they had in the basement, and people are just staring at me.

By the time I’m done, nobody knows what I meant. I don’t always know either. It’s like I had the answer, but it got mixed up on the way out.

When you find yourself copying the beeping or hand signals, do you ever feel like some outside force or person is controlling your movements or making you do it, rather than it just happening on its own?

I don’t know… controlled like by a person? I don’t really have a good word for it.

Sometimes it feels like the beep gets in my body before I decide anything, like when a song gets stuck in your head, except it’s not a song, it’s the forklift backing up, and then my mouth does it or my hand goes up. But I don’t know if that means someone’s making me. I don’t see somebody with a remote or anything.

It’s just… it happens, and then people are looking at me, and then I’m trying to remember if I meant to do it or if it already happened.

At the warehouse I keep doing stuff that doesn’t make sense to them, like freezing there by the forklift with my arms up, and then the beeping starts getting in my head—not in my head, I mean it’s the forklift beeping—and I’ll copy it, or copy the hand signals.

And then the boxes, I’ll start moving them into these little rows or corners, like patterns, even when everyone’s yelling at me to stop. It’s not like I’m trying to mess things up. It just happens, and then people get mad, and the supervisor starts looking at me like I’m dangerous or something.

doctor.intent: Assess whether these episodes are confined to the work environment or also occur elsewhere (e.g., at home), to help distinguish a pervasive neuropsychiatric process (like catatonia or autism-related repetitive behavior) from a context-specific stress reaction or tic disorder.
doctor.question: Do these freezing episodes, the copying of sounds and gestures, or the box-arranging happen anywhere outside of work—like at home or with roommates—or do they only occur on the job?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I guess they brought me in because at the warehouse I keep doing things like freezing with my arms up by the forklift, copying the beeping sounds and hand signals, or moving boxes in strange little patterns even when everyone is yelling for me to stop.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the context and occurrence of the freezing, copying sounds/gestures, and box-arranging behaviors, which are manifestations of disorganized or abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
Mostly it’s at the warehouse, I guess. That’s where people notice it because, you know, there’s the forklift and the beeping and everybody doing those hand signals, and then I’m just… standing there with my arms up, or I start copying it.

At home there aren’t really boxes like that, not the same way. I mean, I’ll put things down and move stuff around, but the thing they brought me in for is work—the rows and corners with the boxes, and people yelling at me to stop like I’m doing it on purpose. It happens there.

inference.note: Symptoms of posturing/freezing, echolalia (copying beeping), echopraxia (copying hand signals), and stereotyped behavior (box arranging) with adult onset (not childhood) point toward catatonic features. No clear evidence of hallucinations/delusions yet, but catatonic schizophrenia (F20.2) and catatonia secondary to another mental disorder (F06.1) remain top considerations. Childhood-onset stereotypy/tic disorders and autism spectrum are less likely given adult onset.

doctor.intent: Assess for an underlying general medical, neurological, or substance-related cause that could explain the catatonic symptoms (to differentiate a catatonic disorder due to a medical condition from primary schizophrenia)
doctor.question: Have you had any recent medical problems—like a head injury, seizures, infections, thyroid issues, or new medications or drug/alcohol use—around the time these episodes started?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about possible medical, medication, substance, or neurological causes around symptom onset, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t… I don’t think there was some big thing like that. I mean, I didn’t get hit in the head that I remember. At work you bump into stuff all the time, pallets and corners and whatever, but that’s just the warehouse, you know?

I’m not really sure about thyroid stuff. I don’t even know what that would feel like. And medications—no, I don’t think there was some new thing right when it started. I don’t really keep track like that.

Alcohol or drugs, no, not like… I mean, people talk about that like it explains everything, but I’m just going to work and then the whole place is beeping and moving and everyone’s mad. I don’t know. I don’t have a good medical answer for it.

inference.note: No medical/substance cause identified, keeping F06.1 as differential; catatonic-like freezing, echopraxia, echolalia, and pattern behaviors persist without clear psychotic delusions/hallucinations or lifelong autistic pattern, so both catatonia (possibly schizophrenia-associated) and organic catatonic disorder remain candidates.

doctor.intent: Assess for other schizophrenia-spectrum features (e.g., negative symptoms like social withdrawal, blunted affect, or disorganized thinking) outside the catatonic episodes, which would support F20.2 over a purely catatonic syndrome from another cause
doctor.question: Outside of these episodes at work, have you noticed any changes in yourself lately—like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, wanting to be alone more, or having trouble keeping your thoughts organized when you talk to people?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: When the supervisor asks me which pallets are going on the truck, I start trying to explain but my words jump from the load sheet to my old house, then fishing, then church boxes, and by the time I'm done nobody knows what I meant.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the patient has trouble keeping thoughts organized when talking to people, which directly matches disorganized thinking/speech.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, talking to people has gotten weird. Like when my supervisor asks which pallets are supposed to go on the truck, I know I’m supposed to just say, you know, “those ones” or whatever, from the load sheet.

But then I start explaining and it goes… sideways. I’ll be talking about the load sheet, and then I’m thinking about the house I used to live in, because the paper had a corner torn like the wallpaper there, and then I’m talking about fishing with my uncle, and then somehow church boxes, like the boxes they had in the basement, and people are just staring at me.

By the time I’m done, nobody knows what I meant. I don’t always know either. It’s like I had the answer, but it got mixed up on the way out.

inference.note: Disorganized/tangential speech (derailment) now reported in addition to catatonic-like freezing, echolalia, echopraxia, and stereotyped box-arranging, strengthening support for schizophrenia (catatonic type) as primary; medical/substance causes remain unconfirmed so F06.1 not yet excluded pending further workup (e.g., thyroid, neuro exam).

doctor.intent: Assess for delusions of control or influence (e.g., believing external forces are making him move/copy involuntarily), which would support a primary psychotic process (F20.2) over a secondary catatonic disorder (F06.1)
doctor.question: When you find yourself copying the beeping or hand signals, do you ever feel like some outside force or person is controlling your movements or making you do it, rather than it just happening on its own?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about feeling controlled by an outside force or person, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… controlled like by a person? I don’t really have a good word for it.

Sometimes it feels like the beep gets in my body before I decide anything, like when a song gets stuck in your head, except it’s not a song, it’s the forklift backing up, and then my mouth does it or my hand goes up. But I don’t know if that means someone’s making me. I don’t see somebody with a remote or anything.

It’s just… it happens, and then people are looking at me, and then I’m trying to remember if I meant to do it or if it already happened.

inference.note: No evidence of a medical/substance etiology (denies head injury, thyroid issues, drug use) argues against F06.1. Presence of echolalia/echopraxia (copying beeping, hand signals), immobility with posturing (arms up), stereotyped behavior (box patterning), and disorganized/tangential speech pattern strongly support catatonic schizophrenia over a secondary catatonic disorder. No clear passivity phenomena or hallucinations reported, but the combination of catatonic and disorganized features with nearly a year's duration fits F20.2 best.
